description: An original retro-style browser platformer built with React, TypeScript, Vite, and Babylon.js.
readme: # Bytebound: Meadow Run > An original retro-style browser platformer built for keyboard and landscape mobile play. [![CI](https://github.com/vincenzo-afk/MARIO/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/vincenzo-afk/MARIO/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-f4b942.svg)](LICENSE) [![Built with TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20with-TypeScript-3178c6.svg)](https://www.typescriptlang.org/) [Play locally](#getting-started) · [Report a bug](https://github.com/vincenzo-afk/MARIO/issues/new/choose) · [Request a feature](https://github.com/vincenzo-afk/MARIO/issues/new/choose) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) --- ## Table of Contents - [About](#about) - [Technology](#technology) - [Getting Started](#getting-started) - [How to Play](#how-to-play) - [Project Structure](#project-structure) - [Features and Scope](#features-and-scope) - [Testing and Quality Checks](#testing-and-quality-checks) - [Deployment](#deployment) - [Contributing](#contributing) - [Security](#security) - [License](#license) - [Acknowledgments](#acknowledgments) --- ## About Bytebound: Meadow Run is an original, route-based platformer. Players run through three handcrafted stages, collect signal shards, activate relay checkpoints, avoid hazards, and reach a portal to advance. The project uses procedural canvas art instead of imported character or sprite assets, so the complete visual language remains original to the game. The game is browser-first and designed for both desktop and touch input. Phones use a landscape play surface with a rotate-to-play handoff in portrait. The install manifest requests fullscreen and landscape presentation for supported mobile web-app environments. | Area | Implemented behavior | | --- | --- | | Gameplay | Movement, jumping, enemies, hazards, checkpoints, shards, portals, lives, respawn, and stage completion | | Level content | Three authored stages: **Meadow Relay**, **Copper Canopy**, and **Dawn Switchyard** | | Controls | Arrow keys or WASD with Space on desktop; pointer-safe touch controls on mobile | | Accessibility and preferences | Left-handed touch layout, sound/music toggle, haptic-feedback toggle, and local preference persistence | | Audio | Original looping music and procedural retro cues for jumps, collecting, stomps, checkpoints, damage, and finishing | ### Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR Player[Player input] --> Host[React GameCanvas host] Host --> Scene[Babylon.js scene bridge] Scene --> World[GameWorld physics and procedural drawing] World --> Levels[Authored stage data] Host --> Audio[Audio and haptic feedback] Host --> Settings[Local browser preferences] ``` The gameplay core is intentionally framework-agnostic. `GameWorld.ts` owns movement, collision, progress, and canvas drawing; `scene.ts` is the Babylon.js bridge; and `GameCanvas.tsx` manages input, touch controls, settings, audio, haptics, fullscreen behavior, and UI. --- ## Technology | Category | Verified technology | | --- | --- | | Frontend | React 19.2.1, TypeScript 5.6.3, Tailwind CSS 4.1.14 | | Game rendering | Babylon.js Core 9.20.0 with a dynamic canvas texture | | Build tooling | Vite 7.1.7 and esbuild 0.25.0 | | Runtime and package manager | Node.js with pnpm 10.4.1 as declared in `package.json` | | Mobile web | Web App Manifest with fullscreen and landscape preferences | | Storage | Browser `localStorage` for player settings | The project has no database, no user authentication, and no required API key for local play. --- ## Getting Started ### Prerequisites Install a current Node.js release and enable Corepack so the declared pnpm version can be used. No environment file is required to run the game locally. ### Installation ```bash git clone https://github.com/vincenzo-afk/MARIO.git cd MARIO corepack enable pnpm install pnpm dev ``` Vite starts the development server using the repository’s `dev` script. Open the local address printed in the terminal. For landscape mobile testing, open the same address on a phone or use browser device emulation and rotate to landscape. ### Available commands | Command | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `pnpm dev` | Start the Vite development server | | `pnpm check` | Run TypeScript without emitting files | | `pnpm build` | Build the browser bundle and production server entry | | `pnpm start` | Run the built production server | | `pnpm preview` | Preview the Vite build locally | | `pnpm format` | Format project files with Prettier | --- ## How to Play Start a route from the in-game prompt. Move, jump, collect signal shards, and use relay checkpoints to preserve progress through a stage. Reach the portal at the end of each stage to continue. | Action | Desktop | Touch | | --- | --- | --- | | Move left | Left Arrow or `A` | Left movement button | | Move right | Right Arrow or `D` | Right movement button | | Jump | Up Arrow, `W`, or Space | JUMP button | | Pause or resume | `P` or Escape | Pause control in the top bar | | Restart a stage | `R` | Restart control in the top bar | | Configure touch, sound, and haptics | Settings control in the top bar | Settings control in the top bar | On mobile, rotate into landscape before starting. The game uses a full-viewport layout on supported browsers; fullscreen is requested after starting and remains optional where a browser does not permit it. --- ## Project Structure ```text . ├── client/ │ ├── public/ │ │ └── manifest.json # Fullscreen, landscape mobile-web metadata │ └── src/ │ ├── components/GameCanvas.tsx # React host, HUD, settings, input, touch controls │ ├── game/ │ │ ├── GameWorld.ts # Physics, progression, procedural canvas drawing │ │ ├── audio.ts # Music and procedural retro audio cues
